annotation.summary_en: Construction workers scheme to sell stolen paint and blame the consumption of thirty buckets on a dog named Kashtan.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a bare, unfinished room filled with oil barrels where two laborers in flat caps are sitting on a wooden bench. One laborer enthusiastically explains a scheme to the other: he has found a buyer for their construction paint, which retails for 10,000 drams, and plans to sell 30 buckets for 5,000 drams each. To cover their tracks when the foreman (prarab) asks where the supplies went, they decide to blame the site dog, Kashtan. They plan to smear the dog's face with paint to make the story believable. Soon, the foreman enters, dressed in an olive jacket and tie, visibly angry that the third floor hasn't been painted. When he demands to know where the 30 buckets of paint went, the laborers claim the dog ate it all, pointing to the dog's colored face. The foreman becomes extremely agitated, shouting that the dog has gone too far, recalling a previous incident where the same animal allegedly ate 50 packs of tiles from the tile-layers.
catchphrases: Արա էս շունը արդեն էստեղսա, արա էս շանը պետքա հանենք, վաբշե ստուց ռադ անենք։
